name: Alcázar of Toledo & Army Museum
story: When the coup failed in Toledo, Colonel José Moscardó shut himself in the Alcázar with Civil Guards, cadets, Falangists and their families, plus a number of left-wing hostages. Republican militias besieged the fortress for 70 days, shelling and mining it until the east side collapsed. On 27 September Varela's Army of Africa relieved it, after Franco had diverted his march on Madrid to do so; the capture of Toledo was followed by killings in the town, including of wounded militiamen in the hospital. The siege became the founding legend of Francoism and the Alcázar was rebuilt as a shrine. Since 2010 it houses the Museo del Ejército.
see: The rebuilt Alcázar, with the Army Museum's Spanish military history galleries; Moscardó's office is preserved and scale models show the fortress before and after the siege.
plan: Museo del Ejército opens Tuesday–Sunday (closed Mondays); allow at least 2 hours. Paid entry, with free periods; check the museum site before travelling.

boxes.text: The famous telephone call in which Moscardó told his son Luis to 'die like a hero' is questioned by historians: some say Luis was shot about a month later, in reprisal for an air raid, not in response to the call. The fate of the hostages inside is also unclear.
